subject: Why negative discrimination value using exploratory mirt

messages.author: 37fd68acfa905f76
messages.subject: Why negative discrimination value using exploratory mirt
parts:
Hi Phil!
      Why do we get negative discrimination value while running an exploratory mirt for extracting one or more dimensions? 
      Is it because of reverse coded items? If so, even after adjusting reverse coded items I have got negative discrimination value (an example is given below).
      I would be grateful if you could clarify my doubt.

      For example, I have given the output of a ten items scale while extracting two factors (each item with four response categories i.e., 1,2,3,4) with an 1810 sample size.

> model1 = mirt(data, 2, itemtype = 'graded')
Iteration: 67, Log-Lik: -12773.176, Max-Change: 0.00009
> coef(model1)

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Why negative discrimination value using exploratory mirt
parts:
It's probably best that you look up linear exploratory factor analysis first, which is the traditional factor analysis using correlation matricies. IRT's exploratory factor analysis is effectively the same, except that dependent variables are modeled as categorical data rather than continuous. The answer to you question is that the coefficients extracted are maximally saturated in that they are only unique up to linear transformations, so negative values appear to reflect this level of saturation. Hence, you would need rotations to find a better orientation, and ideally this solution provides information as to a more constrained 'confirmatory' factor analytic model in the future. HTH.

Phil
